sections.h2: What the Defiance County Recorder handles
sections.html:
Every paper that conveys or burdens land in Defiance County ends up in the recorder's permanent files. The office also accepts military discharge papers (DD214s), keeps them from public view, and issues free veteran ID cards to honorably discharged service members without an appointment.

Filing is the office's job. Staff do not run searches for the public, confirm for you that a mortgage was cancelled, or prepare liens. Anyone may come in and search the public records, and staff will help. An online document index lets a seller look for a recorded mortgage release before listing.

Landowners can also sign up for a free property fraud alert at propertyfraudalert.com, or through the hotline number printed on the recorder's page.

The office charges $34 for the first two pages of a document and $8 for each page after those. A $5 document preservation fee joined the schedule on January 1, 2025, after Ohio Senate Bill 94, which took effect October 24, 2024 and let counties charge up to that amount per document.

Papers that carry their own statutory fees skip the extra $5. The recorder names federal tax liens, state job and family services liens, plats, township zoning documents and UCCs. Recording is paid in cash or by check only. A page counts toward the fee if it has writing on it.

sections.h2: Which approvals does a Defiance County deed need first?
sections.html:
Sellers start at the auditor, because no deed reaches the recorder without the auditor's stamp. The sequence runs like this:

  1. The county engineer's office checks the legal description, locates the parcel on the tax maps and stamps its approval with a date and signature. The engineer's number is 419-782-4751.
  2. For certain splits or subdivisions of less than 20 acres, or with a leftover parcel under 20 acres, the Defiance County Planning Commission must also approve.
  3. A conveyance form travels with the deed. A sale for money pays $4.00 per $1000 at transfer unless an exemption applies, and any deed moving an interest, exempt or not, adds $0.50 for each parcel number.
  4. The auditor confirms that the grantor matches the tax duplicate and that the descriptions agree, then stamps the deed with the fee collected and the parcel count.
  5. The stamped deed goes to the recorder.

A land split adds a tax step. After the engineer approves it, the real estate assessors in the auditor's office work out the tax effect of the split, looking at items such as buildings being transferred and any current agricultural use recoupment charge that may apply to the land. Where a split would leave a parcel under 20 acres, expect the planning commission to be involved too.

Bring these on the day you record:

  • The stamped deed, with its fee paid at the auditor
  • Cash or a check for the recording charge
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope if you want the original mailed back

Call the auditor at 419-782-1926 about conveyance requirements before recording, and 419-784-3111 for property value, sales history and tax questions.

sections.h2: Page and margin rules for a deed
sections.html:
Check the paper against the recorder's list before you carry it in. A printed or typed name must sit beside each signature, and a "prepared by" line must appear (ORC 317.11). Notary seals must be present, the whole document must be in English or come with a certified translation, and pages must reproduce legibly.

  • Ink is black or blue, type is at least 10 point, and nothing is highlighted.
  • The first page keeps a three-inch blank band at the top, and later pages keep one and a half inches.
  • All pages keep one inch clear at the bottom and both sides.
  • Sheets run from 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope goes in for the return.

The county engineer must approve some legal descriptions before recording, and releases and assignments need a legal description. Reference earlier recorded documents when a marginal notation is needed. The office lists a turnaround of three days.

sections.h2: How the county fees relate to the Ohio statute
sections.html:
The county's $34 and $8 figures are the sum of two statutory pieces. ORC 317.32 sets a base fee of $17 for the first two pages plus a $17 housing trust fund fee, and $4 plus $4 for each page after that. The office forwards the housing trust fund share quarterly and divides the rest between the general fund and the technology fund.

The statute also names smaller items a seller may meet. A certified copy costs a base fee of $1 plus a $1 housing trust fund fee per page, a recorder's seal on a certification adds $0.50 plus $0.50, and a marginal reference entered by a separate instrument costs $2 plus $2. Defiance County lists a flat $4 for marginal notations on a release or assignment, so ask which figure applies to a mortgage release you plan to record.

Recording is often done by mail, so the practical points are short. Send cash or a check, add a self-addressed stamped envelope, and allow the three days the office lists for turnaround. A call to the office confirms the total before you mail anything.

Defiance County sits in northwest Ohio along the Indiana line, and the city of Defiance is the county seat and largest city. The 2020 count showed 38,286 people and 16,539 housing units, with 6.4 percent vacant. Of occupied homes, 76.1 percent were owner-occupied and 23.9 percent rented. About 46.4 percent of residents lived in urban areas and 53.6 percent in rural ones, so a seller may hold a town lot or a house on acreage.

Sellers with long-owned parcels should confirm legal descriptions with the engineer before a deed goes to the auditor, since that office will not transfer a deed without the approval stamp. Cash buyers and financed buyers face the same stamp, fee and filing sequence.

Before you list, check the online document index for your mortgage release, collect the numbers for the engineer and the auditor, and decide who will carry the deed. If a title company is handling the sale, ask what it will submit for you and what you must sign in person. Doing this early shortens the gap between signing and recording.

faqs.q: What will a Defiance County deed cost to file?
faqs.a: Expect $34 for the first two pages, $8 for each page beyond those, and the $5 preservation fee in force since January 1, 2025. Pay with cash or a check.

faqs.q: Does the auditor see a Defiance County deed first?
faqs.a: Yes. The engineer approves the legal description, then the auditor collects its fees and stamps the deed, and only then does the recorder file it.

faqs.q: What rate does the Defiance County auditor charge on a sale?
faqs.a: The conveyance fee is $4.00 per thousand and the transfer fee is $0.50 per parcel. An exempt deed skips the first but still carries the second.

faqs.q: Will the recorder's staff correct a flawed deed?
faqs.a: No. The office may not engage in the unauthorized practice of law, which rules out drafting papers or giving legal advice. An attorney or title company should prepare the deed.

faqs.q: Can I look up Defiance County records from home?
faqs.a: Yes, through the online document index in AVA Land Records. A seller can use it to see if a mortgage release was recorded, then visit the office for anything the index lacks.
